title: Two cars at 50, head-on
hook: Two identical cars, both at 50 km/h, meet head-on. What is that crash like for car A?

knows: crashes are worse at higher speed
doesNotKnow: that in a symmetric head-on crash the meeting point stays still, so each car stops from its own speed exactly as against a rigid wall
that crash damage scales with speed squared

misconception: Two cars each at 50 km/h colliding head-on is like one car hitting a wall at 100 km/h.
objective: The learner can explain that a head-on crash between identical cars at 50 km/h is, for each car, like hitting a rigid wall at 50 km/h, because the meeting point does not move and each crumple zone absorbs its own car's energy; a 100 km/h wall puts four times the energy into one car.

claims.text: In a head-on collision of identical cars at equal speeds, total momentum is zero, so both cars stop at the meeting point, which does not move (stage: dashed 'meeting point' line; reveal: 'The meeting point never moved').
claims.source: Momentum conservation: m v + m (-v) = 0 = (2m) v_after, so v_after = 0; by symmetry the contact plane stays at rest throughout. artifacts/scratch/cm-physics-r3/check.mjs (brief claim 1). Brief: company/domains/briefs/physics.mechanics.md round 3 #1. Reveal quote updated in v2 (cm-physics r5 R7); FC pass 35 verification of v1 replaced; reset to unverified for re-check. | FC pass 65 (fact-checker, SO-10-2, 2026-10-16, v2 at 9e7d37c, shared server 987687ac, R3a check pass): VERIFIED. Own node: m*v + m*(-v) = 1500*13.889 - 1500*13.889 = 0, so the perfectly inelastic pair has v_after = 0; with identical cars the contact plane is the centre of mass, at rest throughout. Code: car B is drawn at 2*MID - frontA, so both fronts meet at MID and stop there. Stage: after 'Into a car' a line labelled 'meeting point' appears at MID (class .mid, stroke-dasharray 3 3: dashed), fresh walkthrough step 1. Reveal on :3591 reads 'The meeting point never moved, so each car stopped from 50 to 0 in its own crumple zone, as against a wall.', which contains the quoted 'The meeting point never moved'.

claims.text: Car A's crumple zone absorbs 1/2 m v^2 = 145 kJ at 50 km/h for a 1,500 kg car, the same in a head-on crash with an identical car as against a rigid immovable wall at 50 km/h (stage: 'car 50: 145 kJ', 'wall 50: 145 kJ'; reveal: 'filled car A's crush bar to 145 kJ, as high as the 50 km/h wall (145 kJ)').
claims.source: 0.5 x 1,500 x (50/3.6)^2 = 144,676 J, shown with toFixed(0) as 145 kJ (Demo.tsx `energy`). Head-on: the total 289 kJ is shared equally by symmetry; each car stops from 50 km/h against a contact plane that does not move, which is what a rigid wall does. check.mjs gives 144.7 kJ. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: 0.5*1500*(50/3.6)^2 = 144,676 J -> kJ() '145 kJ'. Demo computes energy(speed) for both targets, so 'car 50: 145 kJ' and 'wall 50: 145 kJ' are identical; the reveal reads runs['car-50'] and runs['wall-50'], both reached milestones. Physics: in the head-on case each car's own kinetic energy is dissipated in its own crumple zone (identical cars, symmetric), same as the wall.

claims.text: A wall crash at 100 km/h puts 579 kJ into car A, about 4 times as much as at 50 km/h, because kinetic energy grows with speed squared (stage: 'wall 100: 579 kJ'; reveal: 'filled it to 579 kJ, 4 times higher'; 'Crush energy grows with speed squared').
claims.source: 0.5 x 1,500 x (100/3.6)^2 = 578,704 J -> '579 kJ'; ratio 578,704 / 144,676 = 4.00 (toFixed(0)). check.mjs gives 578.7 kJ. 25 km/h (also on stage if pressed) gives 36 kJ. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: 0.5*1500*(100/3.6)^2 = 578,704 J -> '579 kJ'; ratio to 50 km/h is exactly 4 -> toFixed(0) '4'. Speed-squared dependence is the formula.

claims.text: Two identical cars at 50 km/h carry twice one car's energy (2 × 145 kJ), and each crumple zone absorbs its own car's half (145 kJ).
claims.source: Head-on at 50 + 50: total kinetic energy 2 x 144.7 = 289.4 kJ, twice one car's 144.7 kJ (0.5 x 1,500 x (50/3.6)^2), absorbed half by each car's crumple zone by symmetry (each car stops from its own 50 km/h against a contact plane that does not move). check.mjs (artifacts/scratch/cm-physics-r3/check.mjs). Reveal (v2, cm-physics r5 R7): 'Two cars at 50 carry twice one car's energy, and each crumple zone takes its own half.' v1 text and its FC pass 35 verification replaced; reset to unverified for re-check. | FC pass 65 (fact-checker, SO-10-2, 2026-10-16, v2 at 9e7d37c, shared server 987687ac, R3a check pass): VERIFIED. Own node: 0.5*1500*(50/3.6)^2 = 144,676 J ('145 kJ' via toFixed(0)); two cars: 289,352 J = 2 x 144,676 (289.4 kJ). Lab frame is the centre-of-mass frame (total momentum 0, c1), so all 289 kJ is dissipated; with identical crumple zones, symmetry splits it 144.7 kJ each, which is each car's own kinetic energy. The model is c5's (identical cars and crumple zones, perfectly inelastic). Reveal on :3591 reads 'Two cars at 50 carry twice one car's energy, and each crumple zone takes its own half.', matching the claim; the '2 x 145 kJ' and '145 kJ' figures are ledger detail and agree with the stage's 'car 50: 145 kJ'.

claims.text: Model: identical 1,500 kg cars and crumple zones, perfectly inelastic, a rigid immovable wall, no braking before impact (stage: '1,500 kg cars, rigid wall').
claims.source: Brief claim 4. Assumption only (not on stage, not in the reveal): with a heavier car the lighter car fares worse, because its speed change is larger (momentum conservation: the pair moves off in the heavier car's direction, so the lighter car's velocity changes by more than its own speed). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Convention, consistent with code: M = 1500 for both cars, symmetric crumple, both stop (perfectly inelastic), wall fixed at MID, constant speed to impact (no braking). Stage label '1,500 kg cars, rigid wall'.

recall.question: Two identical trains, each at 30 km/h, collide head-on. For each train, the crash is most like hitting a solid wall at...
recall.why: The meeting point stays still, so each train stops from its own 30 km/h in its own crumple zone, exactly as against a wall at 30 km/h.
